what: Where the bare-code count started. A check that only reports cannot show a number moving unless something wrote down where it began.
printed_output_reach: covered 2 of 24 CLI commands at capture time - the printed-output guard reaches only `approach evaluate` and `issue receipt`, so a zero read against this baseline is NOT a zero across all printed output. Tracked in printed-output-guard-coverage.
note: Regenerating this is a deliberate act and a reviewable diff. It is never regenerated automatically - a baseline that rewrites itself always equals itself, which is a check that cannot fail.

exposure_to_known_gaps_in_the_check.why_this_is_here: This figure is a registered claim and the release has already corrected three numbers. Measured 2026-08-14, before shipping, so a target of zero is read against a figure whose limits are known. A target of zero against an inflated baseline is a number nobody can act on, and the first person to run it and get mostly false positives is the person who widens the matcher until it catches nothing.

fixed_width_columns.what_the_gap_is: TRC-C8's container test recognises markdown pipe-delimited cells and NOT column-aligned plain text. Run against `compass issue receipt`, this inflated the count 18-fold: 37 flagged, of which 35 were identifiers standing alone in a listing column.
fixed_width_columns.why_the_baseline_is_unaffected: The baseline scans the markdown surfaces in terminology.yml's scan.surfaces. None of them contains fixed-width column layout - that shape only appears in printed CLI output, which this baseline never covered. The gap is real and it is somewhere else.
fixed_width_columns.consequence: The baseline is NOT inflated by this. But it also says nothing about printed output, which is the most reader-facing surface the rule governs. Its reach is markdown documents only.

fenced_code_blocks.what_the_gap_is: Codes inside ``` fences are counted. Most are legitimate quotation - ADR-017 quoting a vocabulary entry verbatim, docs/five-minutes.md showing `G1 Tested before it lands` as sample OUTPUT, a BDD example showing an `@TRC-A1` tag. The quoted-term exception covers a code span; a fenced block is the same act at greater length and is not exempt.
fenced_code_blocks.consequence: Roughly 3% of the figure is quotation rather than unexplained prose. Small, and real.

drift_since_capture.why: This session added S13, S14, the terminology.yml sections and the article passage after the baseline was taken. Drift is expected and is what a baseline is for - it is not regenerated automatically, because a baseline that rewrites itself always equals itself.

exposure_to_known_gaps_in_the_check.what_this_means_for_the_target: Zero is the target for unexplained codes in markdown prose. It is NOT a claim about printed output, and about 3% of the current figure is quotation the check should arguably not count. Both gaps are recorded rather than fixed: fixing either needs a scenario and a mutation proof, which is a separate piece of work. Tracked in receipt-and-scan-container-gaps.

THE_CHECK_IS_STRICTER_THAN_THE_RULE.headline: This check counts EVERY occurrence (466). S7 asks about FIRST USE per piece of output (321). The figure is 31% higher than the rule requires.
THE_CHECK_IS_STRICTER_THAN_THE_RULE.what_S7_actually_says: 'the first time a code appears in any one piece of output, it appears with its plain statement beside it; every mention after that is the bare code, which is shorter and reads better once the meaning is known.' A repeat mention is CORRECT by the rule. This check flags it.
THE_CHECK_IS_STRICTER_THAN_THE_RULE.how_it_was_found: TRC-X5 pointed the check at this issue's own artifacts - documents whose subject IS the identifiers. 428 occurrences against 194 first uses. A spec naming forty scenarios cannot gloss each one forty times, and demanding it would produce worse writing than the defect.
THE_CHECK_IS_STRICTER_THAN_THE_RULE.why_this_is_a_DIFFERENT_failure_from_the: Four numbers were corrected in this release because the MEASUREMENT was wrong - counting the wrong files, the wrong scope, things nobody reads. This one is the first where the CHECK is wrong: the count is accurate and the rule it implements is not the rule that was written. File it separately in your head; the fix is different.
THE_CHECK_IS_STRICTER_THAN_THE_RULE.not_fixed_here_and_why: Fixing it is a matcher change plus a design decision - what constitutes one piece of output for a spec, for CLI output, for agent speech - and by S10 a matcher change stales every mutation proof established through it, all twenty. Deferred deliberately rather than designed at the final gate of a long session.
